Dallas :: Demographics :: part 02 :: chunk_0021
There were 524,498 households at the 2020 estimates,[[81]](#cite_note-US_Census-2020-87) up from 2010's 458,057 households, out of which 137,523 had children under the age of 18 living with them.[[82]](#cite_note-US_Census-2020a-88) Approximately 36.2% of households were headed by married couples living together, 57.2% had a single householder male or female with no spouse present, and 35.6% were classified as non-family households with the householder living alone.[[81]](#cite_note-US_Census-2020-87) In 2010, 33.7% of all households had one or more people under 18 years of age, and 17.6% had one or more people who were 65 years of age or older. The average household size in 2020 was 2.52 and the average family size was 3.41.[[82]](#cite_note-US_Census-2020a-88) In 2018, the owner-occupied housing rate was 40.2% and the renter-occupied housing rate was 59.8%.[[83]](#cite_note-89) At the 2010 census, the city's age distribution of the population showed 26.5% under the age of 18 and 8.8% who were 65 years of age or older. The median age was 31.8 years. In 2010, 50.0% of the population was male and 50.0% was female.[[84]](#cite_note-Census_20102-90) In 2020, the median age 32.9 years; for every 100 females, there were 98.4 males.[[85]](#cite_note-91)

According to the 2020 [American Community Survey](/wiki/American_Community_Survey "American Community Survey"), the median income for a household in the city was $54,747; families had a median household income of $60,895; married-couple families $81,761; and non-families $45,658.[[86]](#cite_note-92) In 2003–2007's survey, male full-time workers had a median income of $32,265 versus $32,402 for female full-time workers. The per capita income for the city was $25,904. About 18.7% of families and 21.7% of the population were below the poverty line, including 33.6% of those under age 18 and 13.4% of those aged 65 or over. Per 2007's survey, the median price for a house was $129,600;[[87]](#cite_note-quickfacts.census.gov2-93) by 2020, the median price for a house was valued at $252,300, with 54.4% of owner-occupied units from $50,000 to $299,999.[[88]](#cite_note-94)

fanoutqa_033763.x:
List of Nobel laureates :: Prize :: chunk_0001
Different organisations are responsible for awarding the individual prizes; the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences awards the Prizes in Physics, Chemistry, and Economics; the Swedish Academy awards the Prize in Literature; the Karolinska Institute awards the Prize in Physiology or Medicine; and the Norwegian Nobel Committee awards the Prize in Peace.[[3]](#cite_note-3) Each recipient receives a medal, a diploma and a monetary award that has varied throughout the years.[[2]](#cite_note-NobelPrizeDescription-2) In 1901, the recipients of the first Nobel Prizes were given 150,782 [SEK](/wiki/Swedish_krona "Swedish krona"), equivalent to 10.8 million SEK in 2023. In 2017, the laureates were awarded a prize amount of 9 million SEK.[[4]](#cite_note-4) The awards are presented in [Stockholm](/wiki/Stockholm "Stockholm") in an annual ceremony on December 10, the anniversary of Nobel's death.[[5]](#cite_note-5)

In years in which the Nobel Prize is not awarded due to external events or a lack of nominations, the prize money is returned to the funds delegated to the relevant prize.[[6]](#cite_note-Winners1942-6) The Nobel Prize was not awarded between 1940 and 1942 due to the outbreak of [World War II](/wiki/World_War_II "World War II").[[7]](#cite_note-PeacePrizeArticle-7)

fanoutqa_024803.t: Persian cat :: History :: Genetic origin :: chunk_0003
fanoutqa_024803.x:
Persian cat :: History :: Genetic origin :: chunk_0003
Recent [genetic research](/wiki/Genetics "Genetics") indicates that present-day Persian cats are related not to cat breeds from the [Near East](/wiki/Near_East "Near East"), but to those from [Western Europe](/wiki/Western_Europe "Western Europe"), with researchers stating that "Even though the early Persian cat may have in fact originated from Persia, the modern Persian cat has lost its [phylogeographical](/wiki/Phylogeography "Phylogeography") signature".[[16]](#cite_note-:0-16)

This can be seen in the [phylogenetic tree](/wiki/Phylogenetic_tree "Phylogenetic tree") of cat breeds and populations. The Persian cat is depicted in red, which indicates it falls genetically in the European cat population. The modern-day Persian cat breed is genetically closest related to the [British Shorthair](/wiki/British_Shorthair "British Shorthair"), [Chartreux](/wiki/Chartreux "Chartreux"), and [American Shorthair](/wiki/American_Shorthair "American Shorthair").[[16]](#cite_note-:0-16) The [Exotic Shorthair](/wiki/Exotic_Shorthair "Exotic Shorthair") is a breed developed in the late 1950s by outcrossing Persian cats with American Shorthairs.

fanoutqa_034019.t: The Lord of the Rings (film series) :: Development :: Move to New Line Cinema :: chunk_0011
fanoutqa_034019.x:
The Lord of the Rings (film series) :: Development :: Move to New Line Cinema :: chunk_0011
As the scripts were taking shape, it became clear that the budget required would exceed Miramax Films' capabilities. The Weinsteins suggested cutting the project to one film.[[24]](#cite_note-CharlieRose-24) Jackson inquired whether it could be around four hours in duration, but Miramax Films insisted on two hours, suggesting major cuts to the story, which Jackson refused. Harvey Weinstein threatened to replace Jackson with screenwriter [Hossein Amini](/wiki/Hossein_Amini "Hossein Amini") and directors [John Madden](/wiki/John_Madden_(director) "John Madden (director)") or [Quentin Tarantino](/wiki/Quentin_Tarantino "Quentin Tarantino"). Jackson believed this was an empty threat to get him to concede to making a one-film version himself.[[27]](#cite_note-Jackson-27)

Harvey Weinstein eventually relented and agreed to put the project into [turnaround](/wiki/Turnaround_(filmmaking) "Turnaround (filmmaking)"), but his draconian conditions were meant to prevent the project from being taken up by another studio.[[27]](#cite_note-Jackson-27) Jackson got an audience with [New Line Cinema](/wiki/New_Line_Cinema "New Line Cinema") CEO [Robert Shaye](/wiki/Robert_Shaye "Robert Shaye"), who accepted the project, but requested that it be expanded into a trilogy. New Line Cinema had many promising reasons that the trilogy would be successful, which led them to sign on.[[28]](#cite_note-28) [Final cut rights](/wiki/Final_cut_privilege "Final cut privilege") were shared contractually between Jackson and Bob Shaye, but there was never any interference in Jackson's cut.[[29]](#cite_note-29) Initially, each film had a production budget of $60 million, but New Line Cinema accepted Jackson's request for an increased budget after a 26-minute preview of *The Fellowship of the Ring* was presented at the [2001 Cannes Film Festival](/wiki/2001_Cannes_Film_Festival "2001 Cannes Film Festival").[[30]](#cite_note-30)[[31]](#cite_note-31)

Bradley entered the [1993 NBA draft](/wiki/1993_NBA_draft "1993 NBA draft") as one of the most intriguing and highly debated prospects in the history of the NBA draft. Supporters claimed his tremendous size and surprising athleticism would allow him to dominate the league. Critics argued that he would struggle in the NBA due to his thin build – listed at just 235 pounds (107 kg), he was described by [Ric Bucher](/wiki/Ric_Bucher "Ric Bucher") of [The Miami Herald](/wiki/The_Miami_Herald "The Miami Herald") as "rail-thin," and [Lee Rose](/wiki/Lee_Rose_(basketball) "Lee Rose (basketball)"), player personnel director for the [Milwaukee Bucks](/wiki/Milwaukee_Bucks "Milwaukee Bucks") at the time, said, "Size-wise, he'll get pushed around a little bit,"[[15]](#cite_note-15) – and lack of experience (just one season of college basketball, followed by a two-year hiatus from the sport due to his church mission).[[16]](#cite_note-16) Ultimately, he was drafted by the [Philadelphia 76ers](/wiki/Philadelphia_76ers "Philadelphia 76ers") with the second overall pick, behind [Chris Webber](/wiki/Chris_Webber "Chris Webber") and ahead of [Penny Hardaway](/wiki/Penny_Hardaway "Penny Hardaway"). Given the novelty of a 7-foot-6 center playing for the 76ers, Bradley was issued jersey number 76.

Philadelphia's management saw Bradley as a major project with huge long-term potential. The team acquired legendary big man [Moses Malone](/wiki/Moses_Malone "Moses Malone") to serve as a mentor for Bradley, hoping to develop his skills in the low post.[[17]](#cite_note-17) Also, the franchise hired strength and conditioning consultant [Pat Croce](/wiki/Pat_Croce "Pat Croce") and registered dietitian Jeanie Subach, as well as assistant coach [Jeff Ruland](/wiki/Jeff_Ruland "Jeff Ruland"), to add bulk to Bradley's skinny frame.[[18]](#cite_note-18) His rookie season (1993–94) produced mixed results. In his first game, Bradley totaled just 6 points and 5 rebounds, but he did manage to block 8 shots in 25 minutes.[[19]](#cite_note-19)

For much of his career, Bradley was inconsistent in scoring and reboundin

"Easy on Me" is 3 minutes and 44 seconds long.[[13]](#cite_note-Apple_Music-13) Kurstin produced the song and engineered it with Alex Pasco and Julian Burg. Kurstin plays [bass guitar](/wiki/Bass_guitar "Bass guitar"), kick drum, and piano. [Tom Elmhirst](/wiki/Tom_Elmhirst "Tom Elmhirst") helmed the song's [mixing](/wiki/Audio_mixing_(recorded_music) "Audio mixing (recorded music)") at [Electric Lady Studios](/wiki/Electric_Lady_Studios "Electric Lady Studios") in New York, and [Randy Merrill](/wiki/Randy_Merrill "Randy Merrill") handled [mastering](/wiki/Mastering_(audio) "Mastering (audio)") at Sterling Sound in New Jersey.[[1]](#cite_note-Notes-1)

"Easy on Me" is a [torch](/wiki/Torch_song "Torch song") song and [ballad](/wiki/Sentimental_ballad "Sentimental ballad")[[14]](#cite_note-Still_No.1-14) which places emphasis on Adele's vocals over piano instrumentation.[[15]](#cite_note-NME_review-15) The song opens with a gentle piano, which intensifies as it progresses, leading into the vocals.[[16]](#cite_note-16)[[17]](#cite_note-Guardian_review-17) Adele's voice mimics this according to *[The Guardian](/wiki/The_Guardian "The Guardian")*'s [Alexis Petridis](/wiki/Alexis_Petridis "Alexis Petridis"), as it "sounds initially wounded, then soars".[[17]](#cite_note-Guardian_review-17) The song almost completely eschews the use of percussion instruments,[[14]](#cite_note-Still_No.1-14)[[18]](#cite_note-18) but a bass drum and bass guitar are played during its latter half.[[19]](#cite_note-Telegraph_review-19) In the chorus, Adele delivers the song title in elongated [vocal runs](/wiki/Vocal_run "Vocal run") and stretches the "e" sound through eight different musical notes.[[19]](#cite_note-Telegraph_review-19) Mikael Wood of the *[Los Angeles Times](/wiki/Los_Angeles_Times "Los Angeles Times")* described her performance as "soaring yet slightly crinkly around the edges".[[20]](#cite_note-20)

In the lyrics, Adele addresses her divorce and asks for forgiveness and understanding from her son,[[21]](#cite_note-21)[[22]](#cite_note-Consequence-22) ex-husband,[[19]](#cite_note-Telegraph_review-19)[[23]](#cite_note-23)

The state of Washington has a temperate climate. The eastern half of Washington has a [semi-arid](/wiki/Semi-arid "Semi-arid") to [warm-summer mediterranean climate](/wiki/Warm-summer_mediterranean_climate "Warm-summer mediterranean climate"), while the western side of Washington as well as the coastal areas of the state have a cool [oceanic climate](/wiki/Oceanic_climate "Oceanic climate") or warm-summer mediterranean climate. Major factors determining Washington's climate include the large semi-permanent [low pressure](/wiki/Low_pressure "Low pressure") and [high pressure](/wiki/High-pressure_area "High-pressure area") systems of the north Pacific Ocean, the continental air masses of North America, and the Olympic and Cascade mountains. In the spring and summer, a high-pressure [anticyclone](/wiki/Anticyclone "Anticyclone") system dominates the north Pacific Ocean, causing air to spiral out in a clockwise fashion. This combination of forces prompted a sharp rise in oil prices to levels far higher than those previously targeted by OPEC.[[110]](#cite_note-110)[[111]](#cite_note-111)[[112]](#cite_note-112) Price volatility reached an extreme in 2008, as WTI crude oil surged to a record US$147/bbl in July and then plunged back to US$32/bbl in December, during the [worst global recession since World War II](/wiki/Great_Recession "Great Recession").[[113]](#cite_note-113)

The university occupies a central location within the city of [Cambridge](/wiki/Cambridge "Cambridge"). University of Cambridge students represent approximately 20 percent of the town's population, which was 145,674 as of 2021, resulting in a lower age demographic in the city.[[55]](#cite_note-56)

Most of the university's older colleges are located near the city centre, through which [River Cam](/wiki/River_Cam "River Cam") flows. Students and others traditionally [punt](/wiki/Punt_(boat) "Punt (boat)") on the River Cam, which provides views of the university's buildings that surround the river.[[56]](#cite_note-57)
